title: Source-grounded verification of the meteoritic-iron [R]/[R-Anker] claims in OTA-FND-0024 ('Die Kette vom Hexenteich') against the primary archaeometallurgical literature
question: Verify the [R]/[R-Anker]-marked meteoritic-iron claims that ground the central artifact of OTA-FND-0024-2026-DE against the primary sources. (a) Are the Widmanstaetten-structure composition ranges (Kamacit Fe + 4-7.5% Ni; Taenit Fe + 20-50% Ni) and the stated Kamacit saturation magnetization (Ms = 1.715 kA/m) accurately reported per the metallurgical/meteoritics literature? (b) Are the cited historical analogs confirmed as meteoritic iron by primary studies: the Tutankhamun dagger (~1350 BCE), the Ugarit bronze-age axes (~1400 BCE), and the Moerigen/Switzerland arrowhead (~900 BCE, reportedly traced to a specific IAB iron meteorite)? (c) Is the document's framing of the artifact as 'eisenzeitliche Glieder' (Iron Age links) archaeologically consistent, given that the archaeometallurgical record of meteoritic-iron use is predominantly Late Bronze Age (before terrestrial smelting) - a material discrepancy the pending OTA-SCI-0059 companion would have to resolve? (d) How defensible is the [T] claim that Monazit/Thorit (Th-232) trace inclusions occur in iron meteorites from the asteroid melt process, given thorium's strongly lithophile geochemistry - i.e., is any Th-bearing mineral phase actually documented in iron meteorites, and what Th/U abundances do iron meteorites carry?
why_now: OTA-FND-0024 declares meteoritic iron (Widmanstaetten structure) the precise scientific foundation of the novel and schedules OTA-SCI-0059 (Meteoritic iron) as an ausstehend companion document. The specific figures (Ni ranges, Ms value), the historical-analog dates, and the eisenzeitlich framing have not been checked against the primary archaeometallurgical record, and the Th-bearing-inclusion premise is a stated [T] hypothesis that can be constrained by meteorite geochemistry.
real_world_anchor: Archaeometallurgical record of meteoritic-iron artifacts (Tutankhamun dagger, Comelli et al. 2016; Ugarit axes; Moerigen arrowhead 2023); iron-meteorite phase diagrams and Th/U trace-element geochemistry.
novelty_reason: No prior OTA research topic audits the meteoritic-iron material claims (Widmanstaetten compositions, Ms value, historical analogs, Iron-Age framing) in any source document. The nearest topic (RES-20260823-273FD1BF) concerns Th-bearing monazite in Levantine/Sinai/Cypriot copper ores and their radiogenic heat, not iron-meteorite mineralogy, so the substrate and claims differ.
